comparison: Both evaluate C105 (MatP5A mutant showing MukE-MatP interaction not essential for inhibition). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED with caveat about single mutant and potential compensation. Peer review implicitly accepts (no critique) but treats as supporting detail rather than major conclusion.

Both evaluate C117-C121 (interplay of replication, MukBEF, and chromosome organization). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED noting progressive CID changes but mechanisms not fully elucidated. Peer review accepts as part of compelling overall evidence without extensive discussion.

Both evaluate C7, C77-C81 (MukBEF activity in non-replicating cells). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED, noting replication not required but facilitates loading. Peer review explicitly affirms with Reviewer 1 calling it 'clear and direct demonstration' that MukBEF can influence organization without replication.

Both evaluate C85-C86, C88-C91 (matS conservation across species). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED but notes evolutionary inference (C86) is speculative. Peer review accepts comparative genomics data without critique, treating high matS concentration near dif as notable finding.

Both evaluate C65-C71 (MukBEF preferential loading on newly replicated DNA via ChIP-seq). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED with 2-4 fold enrichment providing quantitative support. Peer review marks as SUPPORTED despite 'somewhat small effect sizes,' with all reviewers affirming the finding.

Both evaluate C8, C56-C60, C97-C99 (dose-dependent inhibition by matS). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED with clear quantitative evidence. Peer review marks as UNCERTAIN due to Reviewer 3's concern about matS density claim needing 'more systematic studies' based on only two strains with small effect size.

Both evaluate C46-C48 (time-course Hi-C showing progressive long-range contacts). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED with C49-C50 about multiple loading sites well-supported by spatial distribution. Peer review accepts time-resolved experiments as part of compelling evidence enabling subsequent findings.

Both evaluate C9, C93, C109 (MatP mechanism model). OpenEval marks as UNCERTAIN, noting mechanism is inferred rather than directly demonstrated. Peer review marks as SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 2 affirming MatP/matS acts locally to restrict MukBEF, treating model as consistent interpretation.

Both evaluate C82-C84 (identification of 28 matS sites and consensus sequence). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED, noting refined Ter domain map. Peer review accepts without critique as part of comparative genomics findings.

Both evaluate C61-C64, C100 (matS density importance via deletion strains). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED but notes limited sample size (two configurations). Peer review marks as UNCERTAIN with Reviewer 3 expressing concern about comparison of only two strains and inability to factor out sequence composition and genomic context.

Both evaluate C72-C75 (reduced MukBEF enrichment in Ter2 via ChIP-seq). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED as direct evidence MatP/matS prevents MukBEF residence. Peer review marks as SUPPORTED with Reviewer 1 calling genetic rearrangements 'powerful' and evidence 'clear and convincing' for MukBEF exclusion from ter.

Both evaluate C124-C129 (rearranged Ter segments showing no directional translocation). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED, noting separated Ter segments strongly support rejection of translocation model. Peer review marks as SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 1 noting MukBEF can promote contacts between matS zones while excluded from them.

Both evaluate C126, C128 (chromosome rearrangement experiments). OpenEval groups with C52-C54, C124-C125, C127, C129 as SUPPORTED evidence against directional translocation. Peer review focuses on C126, C128 as part of evidence for distributed loading sites, with Reviewer 3 noting rearrangements 'lend strong support' to independence from centralized loading.

Both evaluate C49-C50 (MukBEF loads at multiple loci). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED by spatial distribution of simultaneous contacts. Peer review explicitly affirms with Reviewer 1 stating loading is 'widely distributed' and Reviewer 3 noting strong support for independence from centralized loading site.

Both evaluate C94-C95 (synthesis of findings and comparison to condensins). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED, noting multiple loading sites well-supported and condensin comparison reasonable but mechanistically limited. Peer review marks as SUPPORTED as part of accepted model framework.

Both evaluate C92 (conclusion about multiple loading sites). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED as synthesis well-supported by data. Peer review explicitly affirms with all reviewers and editor confirming evidence is compelling for distributed rather than centralized loading.

Both evaluate C44-C45 (inducible system validation). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED, noting complementation data demonstrate functional system. Peer review treats as validated experimental approach without questioning functionality.

Both evaluate C52-C54 (rearranged Ter segments). OpenEval groups with C124-C129 as SUPPORTED evidence against translocation model. Peer review includes in UNCERTAIN evaluation focused on matS density claims, though rearrangement experiments themselves not questioned.

OpenEval evaluates C4 (background on preferential loading) as part of ChIP-seq evidence for preferential loading on replicated DNA, marked SUPPORTED. Peer review evaluates C4 as part of evidence for distributed loading sites, marked SUPPORTED. Different groupings but both accept the underlying claim.

OpenEval evaluates C1-C3 (background context and study motivation) as SUPPORTED well-established facts. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these are introductory claims not specifically assessed by reviewers.

OpenEval evaluates C107-C108, C112-C116 (discharge mechanism speculation) as UNCERTAIN, noting claims are largely speculative with limited support. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically address these mechanistic hypotheses.

OpenEval evaluates C10-C38, C96, C101-C104, C110-C111, C113-C114 (extensive background literature) as SUPPORTED context from prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these establish scientific foundation rather than novel findings.

OpenEval evaluates C39-C40 (logical framework for Hi-C interpretation) as SUPPORTED reasonable predictions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically assess the experimental logic framework.

OpenEval evaluates C51, C122 (methodological context) as SUPPORTED straightforward descriptions. Peer review mentions C51 in context of genetic rearrangements but does not separately evaluate these methodological claims.

Peer review evaluates C5 (part of distributed loading conclusion) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval does not have a result specifically addressing C5; it may be covered in background context (R17) but not explicitly evaluated as a distinct finding.

Peer review evaluates C6 (MukBEF activity independent of replication) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval addresses related claims (C7, C76-C81 in R9) but does not specifically evaluate C6 as a distinct claim in the same grouping.
